LEDGER & LEDGER LTD.
FRANKING MACHINE FP-2000 – MAINTENANCE MANUAL

Document No: L&L/FM/FP2000/Rev.3
Supersedes: Rev.2 (dated 12 June 2024)
Issue Date: 3 March 2025
Authorised by: P. Whitmore, Facilities Manager

REVISION HISTORY

| Rev | Date | Description of Change | Authorised By |
|-----|------------|------------------------------------------|---------------|
| 0   | 15 Jan 2023 | Initial issue. | J. Okafor |
| 1   | 02 Apr 2023 | Added Section 6 (Postal Rate Update) and revised cleaning frequency in Section 4. | J. Okafor |

| 3   | 03 Mar 2025 | Revised Section 7 service intervals to align with manufacturer guidance; added Section 8 on year-end procedures. This manual remains current for the Franking Machine FP-2000. | P. Whitmore |

---

1. INTRODUCTION

This manual describes the routine maintenance and troubleshooting procedures for the Franking Machine FP-2000 (hereafter "the machine" or "f/m"). The machine is a desktop franking unit used for outgoing post at Ledger & Ledger Ltd's main office and two branch sites.

The Maintenance Manual (S01) states that the Franking Machine FP-2000 has_model FP-2000. Record status: current. This is the current model designation; no other model identifiers apply to units covered by this manual.

All personnel who operate or clean the machine must read Sections 3 and 4 before starting work. Only trained office managers and technicians may carry out the procedures in Sections 5 and 7.

1.1 Safety Conventions

- WARNING: Risk of electrical shock. Disconnect the power lead before cleaning any internal part.
- CAUTION: Do not use abrasive cleaners or metal tools on the print head.
- NOTE: Always keep the manual near the machine for quick reference.

---

2. MACHINE OVERVIEW

The FP-2000 is a self-contained franking unit with an integrated scale, ink cartridge, and electronic meter. It prints a postal impression directly onto envelopes or labels.

Key components:

- Control panel with display and function keys
- Feed slot for envelopes (up to 6mm thickness)
- Label dispenser on the right-hand side
- Ink cartridge housing beneath the top cover
- Weighing platform on the left
- Power socket and USB port at the rear

---

3. INITIAL SETUP

3.1 Unpacking and Positioning

Place the machine on a flat, stable surface within 1 metre of a power socket. Allow at least 10cm clearance on all sides for ventilation.

3.2 Connecting Power

Plug the supplied power lead into the rear socket and then into the wall. Switch on using the rocker switch. The display will show "FP-2000" and then the current date.

3.3 Loading Ink Cartridge

Open the top cover by lifting the front edge. Remove the orange protective cap from the new cartridge. Slide the cartridge into the housing until it clicks. Close the cover. The display will show "INK OK" after a few seconds.

3.4 Setting Date and Time

Press the MENU key, select "Date/Time", and enter the current date and time using the numeric keypad. Press ENTER to confirm. The machine does not adjust for daylight saving automatically.

---

4. ROUTINE CLEANING

Clean the machine weekly, or more often if the office is dusty. Use only the cleaning kit supplied by Ledger & Ledger (part no. FP-CLKIT).

4.1 Cleaning the Exterior

1. Disconnect the power lead.
2. Dampen a lint-free cloth with a small amount of mild detergent solution.
3. Wipe the outer casing, control panel, and weighing platform.
4. Dry with a clean cloth.
5. Reconnect the power lead.

| Revision | Date | Summary of Changes | Authorised By |
|----------|------|--------------------|---------------|
| Rev 7 | 14/03/2025 | Added Section 9.4 re: ink cartridge pressure fault; updated Section 6.2 cleaning interval for label dispenser; revised parts list to include FP-INK2 cartridge. The Maintenance Manual (S01) states that the Maintenance Manual has_latest_revision Rev 7. Record status: current. This is the current controlled revision. | J. Whitmore, Service Manager |

---

## 5. WEEKLY MAINTENANCE

### 5.1 General Inspection

Perform the following checks each Monday morning before the first franking run:

1. Check the power lead for damage or fraying.
2. Inspect the feed slot for paper dust or debris.
3. Verify the display shows the correct date. Adjust if necessary (see Section 3.4).
4. Listen for unusual noises when the machine is idle. A low hum is normal; a clicking or grinding sound is not.

Record the inspection in the office log. If any fault is found, do not use the machine and contact Ledger & Ledger support.

### 5.2 Cleaning the Print Head

The print head is located beneath the top cover, directly above the label dispenser. It must be cleaned every two weeks, or more frequently if print quality deteriorates.

1. Disconnect the power lead.
2. Open the top cover fully until it locks into place.
3. Locate the print head assembly (see Figure 3 on page 14).
4. Use the foam swab from the cleaning kit (FP-CLKIT). Moisten with the cleaning fluid supplied.
5. Gently wipe the print head surface in one direction only. Do not scrub.
6. Wait 30 seconds for the fluid to evaporate.
7. Close the top cover and reconnect the power lead.

**CAUTION:** Do not touch the print head with bare fingers. Oil from the skin can clog the nozzles.

### 5.3 Cleaning the Weighing Platform

The weighing platform should be wiped down weekly with a damp cloth. Do not use solvent-based cleaners, as they may damage the load cell.

If the platform is removed for cleaning, ensure it is re-seated correctly. A small click indicates proper alignment. Misalignment will cause inaccurate weight readings.

---

## 6. MONTHLY SERVICE

### 6.1 Lubrication

The feed rollers and label dispenser mechanism require light lubrication every three months. Use only the silicone grease supplied by Ledger & Ledger (part no. FP-LUBE). Do not use general-purpose oil.

Apply one drop of grease to each of the following points:

- Feed roller bearings (left and right)
- Label dispenser drive shaft
- Ink cartridge housing rails

Wipe away any excess grease with a lint-free cloth.

### 6.2 Label Dispenser Inspection

The label dispenser should be checked monthly for wear. Examine the rubber rollers for flat spots or cracking. If the rollers are worn, order replacements (part no. FP-RLRS).

**NOTE:** The dispenser's cutting blade should be sharp. A dull blade will tear labels rather than cut them cleanly. Replace the blade assembly if necessary (part no. FP-BLD).

### 6.3 Meter Reading Verification

Once a month, compare the meter reading on the display with the reading recorded in the office log. The two should match. If they differ by more than 1 unit, contact Ledger & Ledger immediately. Do not attempt to reset the meter yourself.

---

## 7. TROUBLESHOOTING

### 7.1 Machine Does Not Power On

| Possible Cause | Check | Remedy |
|----------------|-------|--------|
| Power lead not connected | Check both ends | Reconnect securely |
| Wall socket not live | Test with another device | Use a different socket |
| Rocker switch off | Check switch position | Switch on |
| Internal fuse blown | — | Contact Ledger & Ledger |
This section defines the levels of maintenance that may be carried out on the FP-2000 by staff at

the franking machine. Complete all sections of the form before handing it to the Office Manager.

The Office Manager will decide whether the fault can be handled in-house or whether it must be

- Your name and authorisation level.
- The meter reading at the time of the fault (if the machine is still operational).

### 8.11 Safety Guidelines

The following safety guidelines apply to all operators and service personnel. They are not exhaustive. If you are unsure about any procedure, stop work and ask the Office Manager. Do not attempt to improvise a repair or bypass a safety device.

#### 8.11.1 General Safety

- The FP-2000 must only be operated by trained staff. Untrained operators must not use the machine without supervision.
- Keep the area around the machine clear of paper, labels, packing materials and liquids.
- Do not place the machine on an unstable surface. It must be on a level, firm bench or table.
- Do not obstruct the ventilation slots on the rear and side panels. Allow at least 10 cm of clearance on all sides.
- Do not insert fingers, pens, or any object into the label path or the meter slot.
- If the machine emits smoke, a burning smell, or an unusual noise, switch it off at the mains immediately and unplug it. Report the fault on Form FR-1 and refer to Ledger & Ledger.

#### 8.11.2 Electrical Safety

- The FP-2000 must be connected to a 230V earthed mains socket. Do not use an extension lead unless it is a heavy-duty type and fully unwound.
- Do not route the mains cable under carpets or across walkways. If the cable is damaged, do not use the machine.
- Do not plug the machine into a socket that is also serving a high-power appliance such as a heater or a kettle.
- Switch off and unplug the machine before cleaning or before any maintenance task that involves opening a panel.
- If the machine has been exposed to water or other liquid, do not switch it on. Unplug it and contact Ledger & Ledger.

#### 8.11.3 Ink and Cleaning Materials

- Only use genuine FP-2000 ink cartridges. Use of third-party cartridges may damage the print head and will void the warranty.
- Store ink cartridges in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight. Do not store them near heat sources.
- If ink gets on skin, wash with soap and water. If ink gets in eyes, rinse with clean water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical advice.
- Cleaning solvents used for the print head are flammable. Keep them away from naked flames and sparks. Use only in a well-ventilated area.
- Dispose of used cartridges and cleaning wipes in the designated bin. Do not put them in general office recycling.

#### 8.11.4 During Operation

- Do not open the top cover while the machine is printing.
- Do not pull labels from the dispenser while the machine is running.
- If a label jam occurs, switch off the machine before attempting to clear it.
- Do not place heavy objects on top of the machine.
- If the meter reading on the display does not match the office log, stop using the machine and report the discrepancy. Do not attempt to reset the meter yourself.

#### 8.11.5 Service and Repair

- Only authorised service personnel from Ledger & Ledger may open the main casing or perform internal repairs.
- Unauthorised tampering with the meter or the security seal will invalidate the meter licence and may be a criminal offence.

Archive item 2: Photocopier XC-450 Maintenance Manual
Source format: Maintenance Manual

The XC-450 is an A3-capable, multi-function device designed for daily volumes up to 15,000 copies. It is the responsibility of each site's office manager to ensure that the procedures in this manual are followed by all authorised users. Technicians must familiarise themselves with the safety notes in Section 2 before performing any maintenance task.

The manual is divided into two parts:

- Part A: Routine Operation (Sections 2–4) – for daily use by office staff.
- Part B: Maintenance and Servicing (Sections 5–8) – for trained technicians and designated site contacts only.

Where a procedure differs between sites, the site-specific exception log (L&L-LOG-XC450) takes precedence, provided the exception has been approved by the Facilities Manager.

---

**2. Safety Notes and General Precautions**

Read these notes before operating or servicing the XC-450.

1. **Electrical safety** – Disconnect the machine from the mains supply before cleaning internal parts, replacing consumables, or clearing paper jams that require access beyond the front cover.
2. **Heat warning** – The fuser unit can reach temperatures above 180°C during operation. Allow at least 15 minutes for the machine to cool before touching any component marked with the high-temperature symbol.
3. **Toner handling** – Toner powder can irritate skin and eyes. Wear the disposable gloves supplied in the consumables kit. If toner comes into contact with skin, wash with cold water and soap. Do not use hot water.
4. **Lifting** – The XC-450 weighs 82 kg. Do not attempt to lift the machine with fewer than two trained personnel. Use the recessed handholds at the base only.
5. **Ventilation** – Ensure the ventilation slots on both sides of the machine remain unobstructed. Do not place the machine within 30 cm of a heat source or in direct sunlight.
6. **Cleaning fluids** – Use only the cleaning agents listed in Section 6.1. Never use aerosol sprays, alcohol-based wipes, or abrasive materials.

A visual safety check must be carried out each Monday morning before the machine is switched on. The check sheet is provided in Appendix A of this manual. Any fault found during this check must be reported via the usual internal fault-reporting process.

The Maintenance Manual (S02) states that the Photocopier XC-450 has_model XC-450. Record status: current.

---

**3. Daily Operation**

**3.1 Switching On and Off**

1. Press the power switch located on the right-hand side of the front panel.
2. Wait for the startup screen to display "Ready". This normally takes 45–60 seconds.
3. To switch off, press and hold the power switch for 3 seconds, then confirm on the touch panel.

**3.2 Loading Paper**

1. Pull out the paper cassette (tray 1 or tray 2) until it stops.
2. Fan the paper stack to separate the sheets, then align it against the rear edge of the cassette.
3. Slide the side guides until they touch the paper lightly. Do not over-tighten.
4. Push the cassette fully back into the machine until it clicks.
5. For the bypass tray (tray 3), open the cover, load up to 50 sheets, and set the paper size on the touch panel.

**3.3 Making Copies**

1. Lift the document feeder lid and place the original face down on the glass, aligned to the rear-left corner.
2. For multi-page originals, use the document feeder tray. Place originals face up, top edge first.
3. Select the number of copies using the keypad.
4. Choose settings (single/double-sided, paper size, stapling) on the touch panel.
5. Press the green Start button.
**5. Troubleshooting**

The following chart lists the most common faults, their probable causes, and the corrective action to take. Always switch off the machine and disconnect the mains lead before carrying out any corrective action that involves opening the access panels. If the fault persists after the corrective action has been taken, contact the service desk with the error code shown on the touch panel.

| Fault / Error Code | Probable Cause | Corrective Action |
|---|---|---|
| Paper jam in tray 1 or 2 (E-101) | Paper incorrectly loaded, or edges curled | Remove the cassette, fan the stack, re-align against rear edge, reload. Check the paper is within the humidity limits given in Section 2.4. |
| Paper jam in the fuser unit (E-104) | The fuser rollers have picked up the leading edge of the sheet | Open the rear access panel. Allow the fuser to cool for 10 minutes. Gently pull the sheet downwards, towards the floor. Do not touch the rollers. |
| Paper jam in the document feeder (E-110) | Multiple originals fed together, or a staple left in the original | Open the feeder cover, remove the stack, and lift the separation pad. Pull out any trapped original. Check the originals for staples or paper clips before re-loading. |
| Poor print quality – vertical white lines (E-201) | The primary corona wire is dirty | Run the cleaning cycle from the touch panel (Settings > Maintenance > Clean Corona). If the lines persist, replace the corona wire assembly – see Section 7.3. |
| Poor print quality – grey background (E-202) | Toner density is set too high, or the OPC drum is worn | Reduce the toner density by one step on the touch panel. If the fault continues, the drum may need replacement – see Section 7.5. |
| Copy is skewed on the output tray (E-203) | The side guides on the cassette are not set to the paper width | Re-set the side guides so they just touch the paper stack. Fan the paper and reload. |
| Machine will not start (E-301) | The interlock switch on the front door is not engaged, or the mains lead is loose | Check the front door is fully closed and the interlock clicks. Check the mains lead is seated firmly in the socket and in the wall. |
| Machine will not start (E-302) | The fuser unit has not reached operating temperature | Wait 5 minutes and try again. If the error returns, the fuser lamp may be faulty – see Section 7.4. |
| Error code E-401 on the touch panel | The waste toner bottle is full | Replace the waste toner bottle. See Section 6.3 for the correct part number and disposal procedure. |
| Error code E-402 | The staple cartridge in the finisher is empty | Replace the staple cartridge. See the label on the finisher for the cartridge type. |
| Error code E-501 | The hard disk is nearly full | Delete stored scan jobs from the touch panel (Settings > Storage > Delete Jobs). Do not delete system files. |
| Unusual noise from the rear of the machine | A foreign object (e.g. a paper clip) is lodged in the transport path | Switch off and disconnect the mains lead. Open the rear access panel and look for the object in the paper path. Remove it with tweezers if necessary. |

If an error code is shown that is not listed above, write down the code and the sequence of events that led to it, and report it to the service desk. Do not attempt to bypass any safety interlock.

**5.1 Clearing a Paper Jam – Step by Step**

A frequent cause of repeated jams is re-using paper that has been curled or has been stored in a damp environment. Once paper has passed through the fuser, it must be discarded. Do not return it to the cassette.

BookMaster is organised into modules. Each module covers a separate area of the finance function, and your access to each module is controlled by your user role. If you find that a button or menu option described in this guide is missing from your screen, it is likely that your role does not include permission for that action. Please speak to your line manager or the Finance Systems Team if you believe this is an error.

Throughout this guide, we refer to the current version of BookMaster as v4.2.1. If you see a different version number on the login screen, please contact the Finance Systems Team before proceeding – do not attempt to log in to an unapproved version.

2. Getting Started – Logging In

2.1 Opening BookMaster

BookMaster is installed on all company laptops and on the shared office PCs in the finance pod. To open the software:

- Click the BookMaster icon on your desktop, or
- Go to Start > All Programs > Ledger & Ledger > BookMaster, or
- If you are working from home, connect to the remote desktop first and then follow the same steps.

The first screen you will see is the login window. This window has three fields:

- User ID (your six-digit employee number, e.g. 123456)
- Password (the one you set when your account was created)
- Company (this should already show L&L Ltd – leave it as it is)

2.2 Logging In – Step by Step

1. Enter your User ID in the first box. Do not include the leading zero if your employee number starts with one – the system will add it automatically.
2. Enter your password. Passwords are case-sensitive, so check that Caps Lock is not on.
3. Click the Log In button, or press Enter on your keyboard.

If your details are correct, the home screen will load within a few seconds. If you see an error message, note the message text and click OK. The most common error messages are listed below:

- “Invalid user ID or password” – check your details and try again. After three failed attempts, your account will be locked for 15 minutes.
- “Account locked” – wait 15 minutes or contact the Finance Systems Team to reset.
- “Company not found” – contact the Finance Systems Team. Do not try to change the company code yourself.

The Software Manual (S03) states that the Accounting Software Suite has_version v4.2.1. Record status: current.

2.3 First Time Logging In

If this is your first time using BookMaster, you will be asked to change your password before you can continue. Choose a password that is at least 8 characters long and includes a mix of letters and numbers. Do not reuse a password you have used elsewhere.

You will also be asked to select a security question from a list. This is used if you ever forget your password. Please choose a question and provide an answer you will remember – if you forget both your password and the answer, the Finance Systems Team will need to reset your account manually.

2.4 Logging Out

Always log out of BookMaster when you leave your desk, even if you are only stepping away for a few minutes. To log out:

- Click the File menu in the top left corner.
- Select Log Out.
- Confirm by clicking Yes when prompted.

Logging out protects client data and ensures that your session is closed properly. If you simply close the window without logging out, any unsaved work may be lost and the system may not release your user licence for other staff to use.

3. The Home Screen and Module Overview

Once you have logged in, you will see the BookMaster home screen. This is the central hub from which you open all modules and access your daily tasks.

3.1 The Menu Bar

The menu bar runs across the top of the window and contains the main menus:
To open an item from the Task List, double-click it. The relevant module will open and the item will be brought up for you to work on. Once the item is completed, it will disappear from the Task List automatically. If an item stays on your list for more than a few days, this may mean that the task has not been completed properly – for example, an invoice may have been posted but not approved. Check the item details before contacting the Finance Systems Team.

4. The Administration Module

The Administration module is where system-level tasks are carried out. In most offices only the Administration Manager and the Finance Systems Team will have access to this module. If you need something done in Administration and you do not have access, please ask the person in your office who holds that role rather than trying to find a workaround.

4.1 Opening the Administration Module

To open the Administration module:

- Click the Administration tile on the home screen.
- If you do not see the tile, you do not have access. Do not attempt to change your own user profile.

You will be asked to confirm that you want to open the module, because changes made here affect all users. Click Yes to continue.

4.2 User Management

The User Management screen lists all users in the system. You can search for a user by name or by user ID. To edit a user’s details, select the user and click Edit. You can change a user’s name, email address, phone number, and access level. You cannot change a user’s user ID – if a user ID has been set up incorrectly, contact the Finance Systems Team to have it corrected.

To add a new user:

The Software Manual (S03) states that the London Office has_software_license_key BM-2024-8842. Record status: current.

- Click Add User.
- Enter the user’s details, including their full name, email address, and a temporary password.
- Assign an access level. The access levels are described in Section 8.
- Click Save.

The new user will receive an email with their login details and a link to set their own password. This link expires after 24 hours. If the link expires, you will need to reset the password manually.

To remove a user, select the user and click Remove. You will be asked to confirm. Removing a user does not delete their historical transactions – it only stops them from logging in. If the user has unapproved items in the Task List, these will need to be reassigned before the user is removed.

4.3 Backup and Restore

Backups are taken automatically every night at 10:00 PM. The backup includes all ledgers, user settings, and configuration files. Backups are kept for 30 days. If you need to restore a backup, contact the Finance Systems Team – do not attempt to restore a backup yourself, as this will overwrite all current data.

To check that a backup has been taken successfully:

- Open the Administration module.
- Click Backup and Restore.
- Look at the list of recent backups. Each backup shows the date, time, and status. A green tick means the backup was successful. A red cross means the backup failed – contact the Finance Systems Team immediately if you see this.

You can also start a manual backup at any time. This is useful before making major changes, such as upgrading the software or running a year-end close. To start a manual backup, click Run Backup Now. The backup will take a few minutes, depending on the size of your data. You can continue working while the backup runs, but you should avoid posting transactions at the same time.

5. Licence Keys
6.1 Administrator

The Administrator role is the highest level of access available in BookMaster. An
Administrator can perform all actions available in the system, including:

- Creating, editing, and removing user accounts.
- Assigning and changing access levels.
- Resetting passwords.
- Unlocking locked accounts.
- Viewing and editing all ledgers, including the nominal ledger.
- Posting and reversing transactions.
- Running and scheduling reports.
- Configuring system settings, including tax codes, fiscal year dates, and report
  templates.
- Managing licence keys and backup settings.
- Viewing the audit trail.

There is no action that an Administrator cannot perform, with one exception: an
Administrator cannot delete their own account. If the only Administrator leaves the
organisation, a second Administrator (or the Finance Systems Team) must remove the
account and assign a new Administrator.

The Software Manual (S03) states that Tom Hargreaves has_software_access_role
Administrator. Record status: current.

Tom Hargreaves is the named Administrator for the London Office. His account was created
during the initial rollout in March 2024 and has not been changed since. If Tom is
unavailable and urgent administrative action is required, contact the Finance Systems
Team to have a temporary Administrator assigned. Do not attempt to use Tom's login
without his knowledge – all Administrator actions are logged to the audit trail with the
user's name and timestamp.

Administrator accounts should be used only for administrative tasks. Day-to-day
bookkeeping, such as posting sales invoices or reconciling the bank, should be done under
a standard user account. This keeps the audit trail clean and makes it easier to see who
did what. If you are an Administrator and also do routine bookkeeping, request a second,
lower-level account for that work.

6.2 Standard User

A Standard User can perform all routine bookkeeping tasks. This includes:

- Creating and posting sales invoices, purchase invoices, and credit notes.
- Recording payments and receipts.
- Reconciling bank accounts.
- Viewing and editing ledgers, subject to the access rights described in Section 6.5
  (Ledger Access).
- Running standard reports.
- Exporting data to Excel or CSV.

The Software Manual (S03) states that Tom Hargreaves has_software_access_role Administrator. Record status: current.

A Standard User cannot:

- Create or remove user accounts.
- Change access levels.
- Reset passwords (except their own).
- Configure system settings.
- View the audit trail.
- Post transactions dated before the last closed fiscal year.

If a Standard User attempts an action they do not have permission for, they will see the
message "You do not have sufficient rights to perform this action." This message is
informational only – it does not lock the account or trigger an alert.

6.3 Read-Only User

A Read-Only User can view data but cannot create, edit, or delete anything. This role is
intended for:

- External auditors.
- Tax advisers who need to review records.
- Management who need to see figures but should not alter them.

A Read-Only User can run reports and export data, but the export will include a footer
stating "Read-Only Export – not for posting."

6.4 Approver

The Approver role is for users who need to authorise transactions but do not need to
create them. An Approver can:

- View items in the Task List that are waiting for approval.
- Approve or reject purchase invoices, sales credit notes, and journal entries.
- Add comments to an item when approving or rejecting.
## 7. Backing Up Your Data

### 7.1 Why Backups Matter

BookMaster stores all of your accounting data in a single database file. If this file is lost
or corrupted, you could lose months of work. Regular backups protect you against:

- Hardware failure (e.g. a hard drive dying).
- Accidental deletion of data.
- Virus or ransomware attacks.
- Theft of your computer or server.
- Fire, flood, or other damage to your premises.

The golden rule is simple: **if you cannot afford to lose a day's work, back up daily.**
For most small businesses, a daily backup taken at the end of the working day is the
right balance. If you process a high volume of transactions, you may want to back up
more often.

### 7.2 What Gets Backed Up

A full backup includes:

- The main company database (all ledgers, transactions, and reports).
- Your company logo and letterhead templates, if stored locally.
- Saved report layouts and custom report definitions.
- User preferences (e.g. which columns appear in lists).
- The audit trail file.

The backup does **not** include:

- The BookMaster program files themselves. You can reinstall these from the
  installation CD or download them from our website.
- Your Windows operating system or other software.
- Files stored outside the BookMaster data folder, such as scanned invoices you
  keep in a separate folder. If you scan documents and link them to BookMaster,
  you must back up those files separately.

### 7.3 How to Back Up

There are two ways to back up: using the built-in Backup Wizard, or by copying the
data folder manually. The Backup Wizard is the recommended method.

#### 7.3.1 Using the Backup Wizard

1.  Make sure all users are logged out of BookMaster. The backup will not run if
    anyone is still connected to the database.
2.  Log in as an Administrator.
3.  Click **File** in the top menu bar, then select **Backup…**
4.  The Backup Wizard opens. Click **Next** to continue.
5.  Choose where to save the backup. You can select:
    - A local folder (e.g. `D:\Backups`).
    - A USB drive.
    - A network location (e.g. `\\server\backups`).
    - A cloud storage folder that is mapped to a drive letter on your PC.
6.  Type a name for the backup file, or use the default name. The default name is
    `BookMaster_Backup_` followed by the date, e.g. `BookMaster_Backup_2025-03-14.bak`.
7.  Click **Next**. The wizard shows a summary of what will be backed up. Check this
    is correct, then click **Start**.
8.  A progress bar appears. When the backup is finished, you will see a message
    saying "Backup completed successfully."
9.  Click **Finish**. The wizard closes.

> **Note:** The Backup Wizard compresses the data, so the backup file will be
> smaller than the original data folder. A typical small company database of
> 500 MB will compress to around 100–150 MB.

#### 7.3.2 Manual Copy (for Advanced Users)

If you prefer to copy the data folder yourself, for example as part of a wider server
backup routine, follow these steps:

1.  Ensure all users are logged out.
2.  Open Windows File Explorer.
3.  Navigate to your BookMaster data folder. The default location is
    `C:\BookMasterData`. If you are not sure where your data lives, look in
    **File > Options > Data Location** in BookMaster.
4.  Right-click the folder and select **Copy**.
5.  Navigate to your backup location (e.g. a USB drive or network share).
6.  Right-click and select **Paste**. Wait for the copy to finish.
7.  To be safe, open the copied folder and check that the file named
    `Company.mdf` is present and has a size greater than zero.

LEDGER & LEDGER LTD.
FRANKING MACHINE FP-2000 – MAINTENANCE MANUAL

Document No: L&L/FM/FP2000/Rev.3
Supersedes: Rev.2 (dated 12 June 2024)
Issue Date: 3 March 2025
Authorised by: P. Whitmore, Facilities Manager

REVISION HISTORY

| Rev | Date | Description of Change | Authorised By |
|-----|------------|------------------------------------------|---------------|
| 0   | 15 Jan 2023 | Initial issue. | J. Okafor |
| 1   | 02 Apr 2023 | Added Section 6 (Postal Rate Update) and revised cleaning frequency in Section 4. | J. Okafor |
| 2   | 12 Jun 2024 | Updated Section 5 troubleshooting chart; clarified ink cartridge handling in Section 4.2. | P. Whitmore |
| 3   | 03 Mar 2025 | Revised Section 7 service intervals to align with manufacturer guidance; added Section 8 on year-end procedures. This manual remains current for the Franking Machine FP-2000. | P. Whitmore |

---

1. INTRODUCTION

This manual describes the routine maintenance and troubleshooting procedures for the Franking Machine FP-2000 (hereafter "the machine" or "f/m"). The machine is a desktop franking unit used for outgoing post at Ledger & Ledger Ltd's main office and two branch sites.

The Maintenance Manual (S01) states that the Franking Machine FP-2000 has_model FP-2000. Record status: current. This is the current model designation; no other model identifiers apply to units covered by this manual.

All personnel who operate or clean the machine must read Sections 3 and 4 before starting work. Only trained office managers and technicians may carry out the procedures in Sections 5 and 7.

1.1 Safety Conventions

- WARNING: Risk of electrical shock. Disconnect the power lead before cleaning any internal part.
- CAUTION: Do not use abrasive cleaners or metal tools on the print head.
- NOTE: Always keep the manual near the machine for quick reference.

---

2. MACHINE OVERVIEW

The FP-2000 is a self-contained franking unit with an integrated scale, ink cartridge, and electronic meter. It prints a postal impression directly onto envelopes or labels.

Key components:

- Control panel with display and function keys
- Feed slot for envelopes (up to 6mm thickness)
- Label dispenser on the right-hand side
- Ink cartridge housing beneath the top cover
- Weighing platform on the left
- Power socket and USB port at the rear

---

3. INITIAL SETUP

3.1 Unpacking and Positioning

Place the machine on a flat, stable surface within 1 metre of a power socket. Allow at least 10cm clearance on all sides for ventilation.

3.2 Connecting Power

Plug the supplied power lead into the rear socket and then into the wall. Switch on using the rocker switch. The display will show "FP-2000" and then the current date.

3.3 Loading Ink Cartridge

Open the top cover by lifting the front edge. Remove the orange protective cap from the new cartridge. Slide the cartridge into the housing until it clicks. Close the cover. The display will show "INK OK" after a few seconds.

3.4 Setting Date and Time

Press the MENU key, select "Date/Time", and enter the current date and time using the numeric keypad. Press ENTER to confirm. The machine does not adjust for daylight saving automatically.

---

4. ROUTINE CLEANING

Clean the machine weekly, or more often if the office is dusty. Use only the cleaning kit supplied by Ledger & Ledger (part no. FP-CLKIT).

4.1 Cleaning the Exterior

1. Disconnect the power lead.
2. Dampen a lint-free cloth with a small amount of mild detergent solution.
3. Wipe the outer casing, control panel, and weighing platform.
4. Dry with a clean cloth.
5. Reconnect the power lead.

The Maintenance Manual (S01) states that the Maintenance Manual has_latest_revision Rev 7. Record status: current. This is the current controlled revision. | J. Whitmore, Service Manager |

---

## 5. WEEKLY MAINTENANCE

### 5.1 General Inspection

Perform the following checks each Monday morning before the first franking run:

1. Check the power lead for damage or fraying.
2. Inspect the feed slot for paper dust or debris.
3. Verify the display shows the correct date. Adjust if necessary (see Section 3.4).
4. Listen for unusual noises when the machine is idle. A low hum is normal; a clicking or grinding sound is not.

Record the inspection in the office log. If any fault is found, do not use the machine and contact Ledger & Ledger support.

### 5.2 Cleaning the Print Head

The print head is located beneath the top cover, directly above the label dispenser. It must be cleaned every two weeks, or more frequently if print quality deteriorates.

1. Disconnect the power lead.
2. Open the top cover fully until it locks into place.
3. Locate the print head assembly (see Figure 3 on page 14).
4. Use the foam swab from the cleaning kit (FP-CLKIT). Moisten with the cleaning fluid supplied.
5. Gently wipe the print head surface in one direction only. Do not scrub.
6. Wait 30 seconds for the fluid to evaporate.
7. Close the top cover and reconnect the power lead.

**CAUTION:** Do not touch the print head with bare fingers. Oil from the skin can clog the nozzles.

### 5.3 Cleaning the Weighing Platform

The weighing platform should be wiped down weekly with a damp cloth. Do not use solvent-based cleaners, as they may damage the load cell.

If the platform is removed for cleaning, ensure it is re-seated correctly. A small click indicates proper alignment. Misalignment will cause inaccurate weight readings.

---

## 6. MONTHLY SERVICE

### 6.1 Lubrication

The feed rollers and label dispenser mechanism require light lubrication every three months. Use only the silicone grease supplied by Ledger & Ledger (part no. FP-LUBE). Do not use general-purpose oil.

Apply one drop of grease to each of the following points:

- Feed roller bearings (left and right)
- Label dispenser drive shaft
- Ink cartridge housing rails

Wipe away any excess grease with a lint-free cloth.

### 6.2 Label Dispenser Inspection

The label dispenser should be checked monthly for wear. Examine the rubber rollers for flat spots or cracking. If the rollers are worn, order replacements (part no. FP-RLRS).

**NOTE:** The dispenser's cutting blade should be sharp. A dull blade will tear labels rather than cut them cleanly. Replace the blade assembly if necessary (part no. FP-BLD).

### 6.3 Meter Reading Verification

Once a month, compare the meter reading on the display with the reading recorded in the office log. The two should match. If they differ by more than 1 unit, contact Ledger & Ledger immediately. Do not attempt to reset the meter yourself.

---

## 7. TROUBLESHOOTING

### 7.1 Machine Does Not Power On

| Possible Cause | Check | Remedy |
|----------------|-------|--------|
| Power lead not connected | Check both ends | Reconnect securely |
| Wall socket not live | Test with another device | Use a different socket |
| Rocker switch off | Check switch position | Switch on |
| Internal fuse blown | — | Contact Ledger & Ledger |

This section defines the levels of maintenance that may be carried out on the FP-2000 by staff at
Ledger & Ledger Ltd, together with the personnel who are authorised to perform each level. The

### 8.11 Safety Guidelines

The following safety guidelines apply to all operators and service personnel. They are not exhaustive. If you are unsure about any procedure, stop work and ask the Office Manager. Do not attempt to improvise a repair or bypass a safety device.

#### 8.11.1 General Safety

- The FP-2000 must only be operated by trained staff. Untrained operators must not use the machine without supervision.
- Keep the area around the machine clear of paper, labels, packing materials and liquids.
- Do not place the machine on an unstable surface. It must be on a level, firm bench or table.
- Do not obstruct the ventilation slots on the rear and side panels. Allow at least 10 cm of clearance on all sides.
- Do not insert fingers, pens, or any object into the label path or the meter slot.
- If the machine emits smoke, a burning smell, or an unusual noise, switch it off at the mains immediately and unplug it. Report the fault on Form FR-1 and refer to Ledger & Ledger.

#### 8.11.2 Electrical Safety

- The FP-2000 must be connected to a 230V earthed mains socket. Do not use an extension lead unless it is a heavy-duty type and fully unwound.
- Do not route the mains cable under carpets or across walkways. If the cable is damaged, do not use the machine.
- Do not plug the machine into a socket that is also serving a high-power appliance such as a heater or a kettle.
- Switch off and unplug the machine before cleaning or before any maintenance task that involves opening a panel.
- If the machine has been exposed to water or other liquid, do not switch it on. Unplug it and contact Ledger & Ledger.

#### 8.11.3 Ink and Cleaning Materials

- Only use genuine FP-2000 ink cartridges. Use of third-party cartridges may damage the print head and will void the warranty.
- Store ink cartridges in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight. Do not store them near heat sources.
- If ink gets on skin, wash with soap and water. If ink gets in eyes, rinse with clean water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical advice.
- Cleaning solvents used for the print head are flammable. Keep them away from naked flames and sparks. Use only in a well-ventilated area.
- Dispose of used cartridges and cleaning wipes in the designated bin. Do not put them in general office recycling.

#### 8.11.4 During Operation

- Do not open the top cover while the machine is printing.
- Do not pull labels from the dispenser while the machine is running.
- If a label jam occurs, switch off the machine before attempting to clear it.
- Do not place heavy objects on top of the machine.
- If the meter reading on the display does not match the office log, stop using the machine and report the discrepancy. Do not attempt to reset the meter yourself.

#### 8.11.5 Service and Repair

- Only authorised service personnel from Ledger & Ledger may open the main casing or perform internal repairs.
- Unauthorised tampering with the meter or the security seal will invalidate the meter licence and may be a criminal offence.
- Before any service visit, ensure the area around the machine is clear and the office log is up to date.
- After any service, the technician will complete Form FR-1 and leave a copy with the Office Manager.

### 8.12 Disposal Instructions

When the FP-2000 reaches the end of its serviceable life, or is replaced, it must be disposed of correctly. Do not place the machine in general office waste.

The XC-450 is an A3-capable, multi-function device designed for daily volumes up to 15,000 copies. It is the responsibility of each site's office manager to ensure that the procedures in this manual are followed by all authorised users. Technicians must familiarise themselves with the safety notes in Section 2 before performing any maintenance task.

The manual is divided into two parts:

- Part A: Routine Operation (Sections 2–4) – for daily use by office staff.
- Part B: Maintenance and Servicing (Sections 5–8) – for trained technicians and designated site contacts only.

Where a procedure differs between sites, the site-specific exception log (L&L-LOG-XC450) takes precedence, provided the exception has been approved by the Facilities Manager.

---

**2. Safety Notes and General Precautions**

Read these notes before operating or servicing the XC-450.

1. **Electrical safety** – Disconnect the machine from the mains supply before cleaning internal parts, replacing consumables, or clearing paper jams that require access beyond the front cover.
2. **Heat warning** – The fuser unit can reach temperatures above 180°C during operation. Allow at least 15 minutes for the machine to cool before touching any component marked with the high-temperature symbol.
3. **Toner handling** – Toner powder can irritate skin and eyes. Wear the disposable gloves supplied in the consumables kit. If toner comes into contact with skin, wash with cold water and soap. Do not use hot water.
4. **Lifting** – The XC-450 weighs 82 kg. Do not attempt to lift the machine with fewer than two trained personnel. Use the recessed handholds at the base only.
5. **Ventilation** – Ensure the ventilation slots on both sides of the machine remain unobstructed. Do not place the machine within 30 cm of a heat source or in direct sunlight.
6. **Cleaning fluids** – Use only the cleaning agents listed in Section 6.1. Never use aerosol sprays, alcohol-based wipes, or abrasive materials.

A visual safety check must be carried out each Monday morning before the machine is switched on. The check sheet is provided in Appendix A of this manual. Any fault found during this check must be reported via the usual internal fault-reporting process.

The Maintenance Manual (S02) states that the Photocopier XC-450 has_model XC-450. Record status: current.

---

**3. Daily Operation**

**3.1 Switching On and Off**

1. Press the power switch located on the right-hand side of the front panel.
2. Wait for the startup screen to display "Ready". This normally takes 45–60 seconds.
3. To switch off, press and hold the power switch for 3 seconds, then confirm on the touch panel.

**3.2 Loading Paper**

1. Pull out the paper cassette (tray 1 or tray 2) until it stops.
2. Fan the paper stack to separate the sheets, then align it against the rear edge of the cassette.
3. Slide the side guides until they touch the paper lightly. Do not over-tighten.
4. Push the cassette fully back into the machine until it clicks.
5. For the bypass tray (tray 3), open the cover, load up to 50 sheets, and set the paper size on the touch panel.

**3.3 Making Copies**

1. Lift the document feeder lid and place the original face down on the glass, aligned to the rear-left corner.
2. For multi-page originals, use the document feeder tray. Place originals face up, top edge first.
3. Select the number of copies using the keypad.
4. Choose settings (single/double-sided, paper size, stapling) on the touch panel.
5. Press the green Start button.

**5. Troubleshooting**

The following chart lists the most common faults, their probable causes, and the corrective action to take. Always switch off the machine and disconnect the mains lead before carrying out any corrective action that involves opening the access panels. If the fault persists after the corrective action has been taken, contact the service desk with the error code shown on the touch panel.

| Fault / Error Code | Probable Cause | Corrective Action |
|---|---|---|
| Paper jam in tray 1 or 2 (E-101) | Paper incorrectly loaded, or edges curled | Remove the cassette, fan the stack, re-align against rear edge, reload. Check the paper is within the humidity limits given in Section 2.4. |
| Paper jam in the fuser unit (E-104) | The fuser rollers have picked up the leading edge of the sheet | Open the rear access panel. Allow the fuser to cool for 10 minutes. Gently pull the sheet downwards, towards the floor. Do not touch the rollers. |
| Paper jam in the document feeder (E-110) | Multiple originals fed together, or a staple left in the original | Open the feeder cover, remove the stack, and lift the separation pad. Pull out any trapped original. Check the originals for staples or paper clips before re-loading. |
| Poor print quality – vertical white lines (E-201) | The primary corona wire is dirty | Run the cleaning cycle from the touch panel (Settings > Maintenance > Clean Corona). If the lines persist, replace the corona wire assembly – see Section 7.3. |
| Poor print quality – grey background (E-202) | Toner density is set too high, or the OPC drum is worn | Reduce the toner density by one step on the touch panel. If the fault continues, the drum may need replacement – see Section 7.5. |
| Copy is skewed on the output tray (E-203) | The side guides on the cassette are not set to the paper width | Re-set the side guides so they just touch the paper stack. Fan the paper and reload. |
| Machine will not start (E-301) | The interlock switch on the front door is not engaged, or the mains lead is loose | Check the front door is fully closed and the interlock clicks. Check the mains lead is seated firmly in the socket and in the wall. |
| Machine will not start (E-302) | The fuser unit has not reached operating temperature | Wait 5 minutes and try again. If the error returns, the fuser lamp may be faulty – see Section 7.4. |
| Error code E-401 on the touch panel | The waste toner bottle is full | Replace the waste toner bottle. See Section 6.3 for the correct part number and disposal procedure. |
| Error code E-402 | The staple cartridge in the finisher is empty | Replace the staple cartridge. See the label on the finisher for the cartridge type. |
| Error code E-501 | The hard disk is nearly full | Delete stored scan jobs from the touch panel (Settings > Storage > Delete Jobs). Do not delete system files. |
| Unusual noise from the rear of the machine | A foreign object (e.g. a paper clip) is lodged in the transport path | Switch off and disconnect the mains lead. Open the rear access panel and look for the object in the paper path. Remove it with tweezers if necessary. |

If an error code is shown that is not listed above, write down the code and the sequence of events that led to it, and report it to the service desk. Do not attempt to bypass any safety interlock.

**5.1 Clearing a Paper Jam – Step by Step**

A frequent cause of repeated jams is re-using paper that has been curled or has been stored in a damp environment. Once paper has passed through the fuser, it must be discarded. Do not return it to the cassette.

BookMaster is organised into modules. Each module covers a separate area of the finance function, and your access to each module is controlled by your user role. If you find that a button or menu option described in this guide is missing from your screen, it is likely that your role does not include permission for that action. Please speak to your line manager or the Finance Systems Team if you believe this is an error.

Throughout this guide, we refer to the current version of BookMaster as v4.2.1. 2. Getting Started – Logging In

2.1 Opening BookMaster

BookMaster is installed on all company laptops and on the shared office PCs in the finance pod. To open the software:

- Click the BookMaster icon on your desktop, or
- Go to Start > All Programs > Ledger & Ledger > BookMaster, or
- If you are working from home, connect to the remote desktop first and then follow the same steps.

The first screen you will see is the login window. This window has three fields:

- User ID (your six-digit employee number, e.g. 123456)
- Password (the one you set when your account was created)
- Company (this should already show L&L Ltd – leave it as it is)

2.2 Logging In – Step by Step

1. Enter your User ID in the first box. Do not include the leading zero if your employee number starts with one – the system will add it automatically.
2. Enter your password. Passwords are case-sensitive, so check that Caps Lock is not on.
3. Click the Log In button, or press Enter on your keyboard.

If your details are correct, the home screen will load within a few seconds. If you see an error message, note the message text and click OK. The most common error messages are listed below:

- “Invalid user ID or password” – check your details and try again. After three failed attempts, your account will be locked for 15 minutes.
- “Account locked” – wait 15 minutes or contact the Finance Systems Team to reset.
- “Company not found” – contact the Finance Systems Team. Do not try to change the company code yourself.

The Software Manual (S03) states that the Accounting Software Suite has_version v4.2.1. Record status: current.

2.3 First Time Logging In

If this is your first time using BookMaster, you will be asked to change your password before you can continue. Choose a password that is at least 8 characters long and includes a mix of letters and numbers. Do not reuse a password you have used elsewhere.

You will also be asked to select a security question from a list. This is used if you ever forget your password. Please choose a question and provide an answer you will remember – if you forget both your password and the answer, the Finance Systems Team will need to reset your account manually.

2.4 Logging Out

Always log out of BookMaster when you leave your desk, even if you are only stepping away for a few minutes. To log out:

- Click the File menu in the top left corner.
- Select Log Out.
- Confirm by clicking Yes when prompted.

Logging out protects client data and ensures that your session is closed properly. If you simply close the window without logging out, any unsaved work may be lost and the system may not release your user licence for other staff to use.

3. The Home Screen and Module Overview

Once you have logged in, you will see the BookMaster home screen. This is the central hub from which you open all modules and access your daily tasks.

3.1 The Menu Bar

The menu bar runs across the top of the window and contains the main menus:

6.1 Administrator

The Administrator role is the highest level of access available in BookMaster. An
Administrator can perform all actions available in the system, including:

- Creating, editing, and removing user accounts.
- Assigning and changing access levels.
- Resetting passwords.
- Unlocking locked accounts.
- Viewing and editing all ledgers, including the nominal ledger.
- Posting and reversing transactions.
- Running and scheduling reports.
- Configuring system settings, including tax codes, fiscal year dates, and report
  templates.
- Managing licence keys and backup settings.
- Viewing the audit trail.

There is no action that an Administrator cannot perform, with one exception: an
Administrator cannot delete their own account. If the only Administrator leaves the
organisation, a second Administrator (or the Finance Systems Team) must remove the
account and assign a new Administrator.

The Software Manual (S03) states that Tom Hargreaves has_software_access_role
Administrator. Record status: current.

Tom Hargreaves is the named Administrator for the London Office. His account was created
during the initial rollout in March 2024 and has not been changed since. If Tom is
unavailable and urgent administrative action is required, contact the Finance Systems
Team to have a temporary Administrator assigned. Do not attempt to use Tom's login
without his knowledge – all Administrator actions are logged to the audit trail with the
user's name and timestamp.

Administrator accounts should be used only for administrative tasks. Day-to-day
bookkeeping, such as posting sales invoices or reconciling the bank, should be done under
a standard user account. This keeps the audit trail clean and makes it easier to see who
did what. If you are an Administrator and also do routine bookkeeping, request a second,
lower-level account for that work.

6.2 Standard User

A Standard User can perform all routine bookkeeping tasks. This includes:

- Creating and posting sales invoices, purchase invoices, and credit notes.
- Recording payments and receipts.
- Reconciling bank accounts.
- Viewing and editing ledgers, subject to the access rights described in Section 6.5
  (Ledger Access).
- Running standard reports.
- Exporting data to Excel or CSV.

The Software Manual (S03) states that Tom Hargreaves has_software_access_role Administrator. Record status: current.

A Standard User cannot:

- Create or remove user accounts.
- Change access levels.
- Reset passwords (except their own).
- Configure system settings.
- View the audit trail.
- Post transactions dated before the last closed fiscal year.

If a Standard User attempts an action they do not have permission for, they will see the
message "You do not have sufficient rights to perform this action." This message is
informational only – it does not lock the account or trigger an alert.

6.3 Read-Only User

A Read-Only User can view data but cannot create, edit, or delete anything. This role is
intended for:

- External auditors.
- Tax advisers who need to review records.
- Management who need to see figures but should not alter them.

A Read-Only User can run reports and export data, but the export will include a footer
stating "Read-Only Export – not for posting."

6.4 Approver

The Approver role is for users who need to authorise transactions but do not need to
create them. An Approver can:

- View items in the Task List that are waiting for approval.
- Approve or reject purchase invoices, sales credit notes, and journal entries.
- Add comments to an item when approving or rejecting.

## 7. Backing Up Your Data

### 7.1 Why Backups Matter

BookMaster stores all of your accounting data in a single database file. If this file is lost
or corrupted, you could lose months of work. Regular backups protect you against:

- Hardware failure (e.g. a hard drive dying).
- Accidental deletion of data.
- Virus or ransomware attacks.
- Theft of your computer or server.
- Fire, flood, or other damage to your premises.

The golden rule is simple: **if you cannot afford to lose a day's work, back up daily.**
For most small businesses, a daily backup taken at the end of the working day is the
right balance. If you process a high volume of transactions, you may want to back up
more often.

### 7.2 What Gets Backed Up

A full backup includes:

- The main company database (all ledgers, transactions, and reports).
- Your company logo and letterhead templates, if stored locally.
- Saved report layouts and custom report definitions.
- User preferences (e.g. which columns appear in lists).
- The audit trail file.

The backup does **not** include:

- The BookMaster program files themselves. You can reinstall these from the
  installation CD or download them from our website.
- Your Windows operating system or other software.
- Files stored outside the BookMaster data folder, such as scanned invoices you
  keep in a separate folder. If you scan documents and link them to BookMaster,
  you must back up those files separately.

### 7.3 How to Back Up

There are two ways to back up: using the built-in Backup Wizard, or by copying the
data folder manually. The Backup Wizard is the recommended method.

#### 7.3.1 Using the Backup Wizard

1.  Make sure all users are logged out of BookMaster. The backup will not run if
    anyone is still connected to the database.
2.  Log in as an Administrator.
3.  Click **File** in the top menu bar, then select **Backup…**
4.  The Backup Wizard opens. Click **Next** to continue.
5.  Choose where to save the backup. You can select:
    - A local folder (e.g. `D:\Backups`).
    - A USB drive.
    - A network location (e.g. `\\server\backups`).
    - A cloud storage folder that is mapped to a drive letter on your PC.
6.  Type a name for the backup file, or use the default name. The default name is
    `BookMaster_Backup_` followed by the date, e.g. `BookMaster_Backup_2025-03-14.bak`.
7.  Click **Next**. The wizard shows a summary of what will be backed up. Check this
    is correct, then click **Start**.
8.  A progress bar appears. When the backup is finished, you will see a message
    saying "Backup completed successfully."
9.  Click **Finish**. The wizard closes.

> **Note:** The Backup Wizard compresses the data, so the backup file will be
> smaller than the original data folder. A typical small company database of
> 500 MB will compress to around 100–150 MB.

#### 7.3.2 Manual Copy (for Advanced Users)

If you prefer to copy the data folder yourself, for example as part of a wider server
backup routine, follow these steps:

1.  Ensure all users are logged out.
2.  Open Windows File Explorer.
3.  Navigate to your BookMaster data folder. The default location is
    `C:\BookMasterData`. If you are not sure where your data lives, look in
    **File > Options > Data Location** in BookMaster.
4.  Right-click the folder and select **Copy**.
5.  Navigate to your backup location (e.g. a USB drive or network share).
6.  Right-click and select **Paste**. Wait for the copy to finish.
7.  To be safe, open the copied folder and check that the file named
    `Company.mdf` is present and has a size greater than zero.
